statement.p: Calculate the integral of f(x,y)=8 x over the region \mathcal{D} bounded above by y=x(2-x) and below by x=y(2-y).
Hint: Apply the quadratic formula to the lower boundary curve to solve for y as a function of x.

static.solution:
y=x, thus their point of intersection is ( 1,1 ).
The region \mathcal{D} is shown in the following figure:
To find the inequalities defining the region \mathcal{D} as a vertically simple region,
we first must solve the lower boundary curve for y in terms of x. We get x=y( 2-y )=2y-{y}^2 {y}^2-2y+x=0 We solve the quadratic equation in y: y=1\pm \sqrt{1-x}
The domain \mathcal{D} lies below the line y=1, hence the appropriate solution is y=1-\sqrt{1-x}.
We obtain the following inequalities for \mathcal{D}: 0\le x\le 1,\quad 1-\sqrt{1-x}\le y\le x( 2-x ) We now evaluate the double integral of f( x,y )=8 x over \mathcal{D}: \begin{array}{rcl} \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 8 x \,dA \amp =\amp \int_0^1 \int_{1-\sqrt{1-x}}^{x( 2-x )}8 x \,dy \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 8 xy\bigg|_{y=1-\sqrt{1-x}}^{x( 2-x )}\,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 8 \left({x}^2( 2-x )-\left(x-x\sqrt{1-x}\right)\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp \int_0^1 8 \left(2{x}^2-{x}^3-x+x\sqrt{1-x}\right) \,dx\\ \amp =\amp 8\left(\frac{2{x}^3}{3}-\frac{{x}^4}{4}-\frac{{x}^2}{2}\right)\bigg|_0^1+8\int_0^1x\sqrt{1-x}\,dx\\ \amp =\amp -\frac{8}{12}+8\int_0^1 x\sqrt{1-x} \,dx \end{array} Using the substitution u=1-x it can be shown that \int_0^1 x\sqrt{1-x} \,dx=\frac{4}{15}.
Therefore we get \int\!\!\int _{\mathcal{D}} 8 x \,dA= -\frac{8}{12}+\frac{32}{15}=\frac{88}{60}=1.46667
